chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinān, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying:

If a man does not find a means of purification and he is in janabah, then let him wipe from the earth and pray. Then when he finds water, let him perform ghusl, and the prayer that he performed has sufficed him.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَتْهُ: it was sufficient and fulfilled the obligation for him
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the earth, used as the medium for tayammum
key_terms.جُنُبًا: being in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.فَلْيَغْتَسِلْ: let him perform ghusl upon finding water
key_terms.فَلْيَمْسَحْ: let him perform wiping, referring here to tayammum

ai.seo_question: If a junub person prays with tayammum and later finds water, must the prayer be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when a person in janabah cannot find water, he performs tayammum with the earth and offers his salat. If he later finds water, he must perform ghusl, but he does not have to repeat the prayer already performed.
